clue.text: Singular poem about flowers

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the two words are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A remarkable poem written on the subject of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it means 'on the subject of', but it is the anagram signal: the letters of SINGULAR and POEM, rearranged, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelargoniums are the plants often called geraniums, grown for their bright blooms.

clue.text: Capricious boy captures deserter

indicators.note: captures means one word holds another inside it

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A whimsical lad catches an army runaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'captures' as an arrest; as the indicator it means the boy's name surrounds the rat. A rat deserting is the old image of rats leaving a sinking ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe behaviour that is unpredictable and changes without warning.

clue.text: Note the orchestration in "My Way"-it's a gem!

parts.note: A is a musical note

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word my

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: orchestration means arranging music, so the letters of the word the are arranged anew

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A remark about the arrangement of the song My Way, praised as a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orchestration' rearranges the word the into ETH; 'in' then sets it within the word my. The song title is a distraction: only its first word is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple quartz used as a precious stone.

clue.text: No gold for a month? That's a blow!

indicators.note: No here means the month is without the letters for gold

parts.note: August is a month
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A month without any money would be a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A gust is a sudden blast of wind, which blows.

clue.text: The French want employment outside — some form of handicraft

indicators.note: outside means the two words go round the French article

parts.note: to want something is to need it
employment is work
le is the French for 'the'

explanation.surface: The French want a job abroad doing crafts.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the French needing work; 'outside' instead makes the two English words wrap the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Needlework is sewing or embroidery, a craft done by hand.

clue.text: Less than fifty per cent from all-rounder

indicators.note: fifty per cent means half of the letters of the word are taken, here the back half

explanation.surface: A cricketer who bats and bowls who scores less than half.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLROUNDER has ten letters; its last five give the answer. An all-rounder is a cricketer who both bats and bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: Under means below a figure, as in 'under ten'.

clue.text: Short cut on the beach

explanation.definitionFit: A shingle is a short bobbed haircut of the 1920s; shingle is also the pebbles on a beach.

clue.text: Unending complaint: only males have time for personality disorder

indicators.note: unending means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a malady is an illness or complaint
just means only
men are males

explanation.surface: Endless moaning from men alone over time hints at a troubled mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unending' drops the final letter of the complaint; the remaining pieces simply follow in order, with 'have' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladjustment is a failure to cope with one's surroundings, a disturbed character.

clue.text: Closet agility coming out in a selfish manner

indicators.note: coming out suggests the letters break free and form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A secretly nimble person reveals themselves in a self-centred way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' reads as revealing a secret, but it is the anagram signal for CLOSET and AGILITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotistically means acting with excessive self-importance, putting oneself first.

clue.text: Stuffy and out of tune?

explanation.definitionFit: A stuffy room lacks fresh breeze; read as 'air-less', it means without a melody.

clue.text: Engine drivers start running out of steam — like water going down the plughole

definitions.text: like water going down the plughole

indicators.note: start means the opening letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: something running out of steam is dying

explanation.surface: Train drivers find their engines losing power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes E and D from 'Engine drivers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Water swirling down a drain moves in a whirlpool, circling as it goes.

clue.text: One yearning for a letter

parts.note: a means one
an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: Someone longing to receive a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is how the letter H is named.

clue.text: OK, there's nothing left

explanation.definitionFit: All right means satisfactory; read as 'all on the right', nothing is on the left side.

clue.text: Fruit growers start to hire again before the first of September

indicators.note: start means the first letter of the word growers

parts.note: to re-engage someone is to hire them again

indicators.note: the first of means the opening letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: Fruit farmers plan to rehire pickers before September.
explanation.walkthrough: G (from 'growers start'), REENGAGE and S (from 'the first of September') join up.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a kind of green plum.

clue.text: Home secretary's spillikins

explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was Home Secretary, the British minister for policing and immigration, from 1997 to 2001; his name plus the possessive S spells the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Spillikins is a game of picking thin sticks from a pile one at a time; the first half names a former British cabinet minister.

clue.text: Somewhere to eat a pickle or jam

explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a dining hall for service personnel; a pickle and a jam are both tight spots or muddles.

clue.text: Self-willed poet's rate of pay?

explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means contrary and stubborn; 'per verse' would be the payment rate for each stanza.

clue.text: Hence double 13

indicators.note: double means the word appears twice in succession

parts.note: so means therefore, hence

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: therefore, twice the earlier clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 refers to the answer ALL RIGHT at 13 across.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means passable or middling, just about acceptable.

clue.text: What a volunteer does, having seen portents in the sky?

definitions.text: having seen portents in the sky?

explanation.definitionFit: To sign up is to enlist; read literally, omens appear overhead.

clue.text: Indian turned inside out gets provisional order for divorce

indicators.note: turned signals that the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: An Indian person turns their clothes inside out on receiving divorce papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges the people's name together with the clue's word 'inside', while 'out' extends the surface picture of clothes inside out. The answer is a British legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree nisi is the interim court ruling before a marriage is finally dissolved.

clue.text: Climbers holding gold keys

indicators.note: holding means one word contains the other

parts.note: ivies are climbing plants
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbers' suggests mountaineers but means plants; 'holding' puts the heraldic gold within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were traditionally made of ivory, so they are called the ivories.

clue.text: A simpleton, that's me, admitting midnight robberies

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: muggins is a self-mocking name for oneself as a fool
the middle letter of the word night

explanation.surface: A fool confesses to night-time thefts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' puts G, the middle of 'night', inside MUGGINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggings are street assaults in which victims are robbed.

clue.text: A little porpoise reared in a tributary of the Rhone

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small porpoise was brought up in a French river.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'in' in the definition; it is a link word, since 'a tributary of the Rhone' alone is the noun the answer replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isère is a river in south-east France that flows into the Rhône.

clue.text: A flower for a member of the string quartet

definitions.text: a member of the string quartet

explanation.definitionFit: A viola is a pansy-like bloom and also the stringed instrument between violin and cello.

clue.text: Primate starting sermon in recess at eastern end of church

definitions.text: recess at eastern end of church

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: an ape is a primate

indicators.note: starting means the first letter of the word sermon

explanation.surface: An archbishop begins his sermon in the church recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, but here it is an ape; 'in' puts S inside APE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular vaulted end of a church.

clue.text: Revolutionary obtains inside information, making savings

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the built word is read backwards
inside puts one word within another

parts.note: gen is slang for information
to obtain is to get, so obtains is gets

explanation.surface: A rebel acquires secret intelligence and builds up funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' sets the word for obtains within the slang for information, giving GGETSEN; 'Revolutionary' then reads the whole backwards. 'Revolutionary' looks like the subject, not an indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is money put aside for the future.

clue.text: Not just incomplete

explanation.definitionFit: Partial means biased, so unfair; it also means only in part.

clue.text: Document for publication found in iron shed

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
to shed is to let go, release

explanation.surface: A notice for the newspapers turns up in an ironing shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A press release is a statement issued to journalists.
